pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Close the two concrete consequence-bearing defects reproduced during the final aggregate CAP Core-v1 freeze audit of #165..#174.

This PR is stacked on #174 exact head:

`e4f09644c8f1b85017c4a49e3073e12877cd236d`

## Finding 1 — Browser UNKNOWN could redeliver

The direct semantic Browser authorizer is intentionally stateless per call. A delivered click/type/navigation that ended without a verified PASS could therefore be followed by another public call, a fresh snapshot, a fresh exact grant, and another physical mutation.

The previous "already satisfied" preflight only prevented duplicate delivery when the expected state had become observable. It did not close the UNKNOWN/unverified case.

### Correction

One-way semantic-activation mutation quarantine:

- after any proven Browser delivery attempt that does not finish with verified PASS, the current semantic activation is mutation-quarantined;
- later `web_open` and `web_interact` calls fail closed before authorization/provider delivery;
- `web_observe` remains available;
- there is no clear/retry/reconciliation API and no automatic continuation;
- no public schema changes.

The regression test uses the real CAP authorizer and semantic path, injects only an ambiguous verifier result, proves the first physical side effect happened, proves read-only observation remains possible, and proves a second click plus later navigation are blocked.

## Finding 2 — workspace failure rollback bypassed authorization

The normal workspace transition path was exact-grant authorized, but failure/finally compensation could still physically delete verified-owned staging/target files directly.

Ownership proof is not authority.

### Correction

Remove automatic failure-path physical compensation.

On failure:

- any verified-owned residual staging/target object is left in place;
- checkpoint evidence reports it truthfully;
- normal authorized successful `staging_cleanup` remains unchanged;
- future automatic cleanup, if desired, must be a separately reviewed authorized operation.

The same hidden rollback behavior is removed from both the active runtime module and the parallel support implementation.

## Stage Research

Added:

`project-context/CORE_V1_FREEZE_AUDIT_FINDINGS_REENTRY.md`

Decision: **NARROW**.

No WorkingState persistence is added to ordinary Browser calls; no new rollback actions are introduced; no registry, scheduler, policy engine, provider framework, public tool or Rust Native Host is added.

## Freeze invariants added

The Core-v1 manifest now explicitly records:

- unresolved direct semantic mutation fails closed before later physical mutation in the same active semantic scope;
- failure compensation is itself consequence-bearing and cannot bypass authorization merely because an object is verified-owned.

## Acceptance

Added/extended tests prove:

- Browser UNKNOWN/unverified delivery cannot be followed by a second physical mutation in the same activation;
- `web_observe` remains available after quarantine;
- PASS does not quarantine;
- workspace forced failures after stage/final verification do not physically delete owned files;
- freeze-surface tests reject reintroduction of hidden rollback compensation or missing Browser quarantine.

This PR must remain Draft and must not merge before the prerequisite Core stack is accepted/refreshed. A fresh independent aggregate freeze audit is required on the new exact head.
